summary: Supply-chain planning domain foundation adds consensus demand-plan approval, supply-network plan proposal metadata, available-to-promise response metadata, distribution-lane plan metadata, and SAP SCM/APO parity-map linkage while explicitly refusing durable persistence, live planning solver execution, demand-sensing ML runtime, production order creation, procurement requisitions, inventory mutation, warehouse reservation, order-management rescheduling, carrier booking, Workflow execution, cloud deployment, and runtime audit-chain claims.
non_claims: no planning optimizer or finite scheduler runtime
no ATP or CTP runtime engine
no inventory mutation or warehouse reservation
no carrier booking or transportation execution

findings: The slice is additive and isolates supply-chain-planning domain invariants in a flat microservice crate rather than widening Enterprise Suite into an ERP/APO monolith.
The API remains pure data-in/data-out with no I/O, durable state, network clients, solver runtime, scheduler runtime, or execution-side mutations.

claims_allowed: ERP parity-map linkage for SAP SCM/APO
findings: Independent scaling and deployment remain future adapter/runtime work; this slice only creates the pure domain foundation.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if missing demand-plan approval, missing supply-plan proposal, unsafe refs, credential-shaped evidence refs, invalid dates, invalid horizons, invalid lead times, invalid priorities, zero quantities, insufficient lane capacity, or shortage overclaims are accepted.
findings: Positive demand-to-supply-to-ATP-to-distribution flow and negative guard rails are covered.
Types map directly to demand plans, supply plans, available-to-promise responses, and distribution-lane plans common to ERP supply-chain-planning systems.

alternatives_named: leave SCM/APO as a parity gap
build live IBP/APO optimizer, ATP/CTP, and transportation runtime now
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A flat domain foundation gives SCM/APO parity a service-owned first write path while keeping planning solvers, finite scheduling, demand-sensing ML, order-management mutation, inventory/warehouse mutation, transportation execution, Workflow, durable state, and cloud adapters out of scope.
rejected_reasons: Leaving SCM/APO as a gap weakens ERP parity after procurement, warehouse, production-planning, quality, and plant-maintenance foundations landed.
Live planning runtime requires durable planning data, optimization/scheduling engines, order/inventory integrations, transport execution, operational SLOs, and cloud evidence beyond this slice.

findings: No credentials, external network calls, planning engine calls, inventory mutations, order-management mutations, carrier bookings, or Workflow dispatches are introduced.
Source and audit refs reject traversal, whitespace/control, and credential-shaped strings.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: Pure string/date/quantity validation and bounded arithmetic only; no I/O or unbounded data access exists.

findings.summary: No database, network, filesystem, optimizer, scheduler, ML runtime, carrier connector, or hot runtime path is introduced.

data_class_touched: FINANCIAL forecast, order, inventory, capacity, lot size, promise, transfer, freight, and shortage quantities
findings: SAP, Oracle, and Microsoft official materials inform supply-chain-planning coverage only; no exhaustive vendor parity or proprietary behavior clone is claimed.
The change is additive: one new crate/spec/catalog row and parity-map references; no migration or external resource is introduced.
Static evidence, task rows, and audit-chain rows document the change; runtime audit emission remains a non-claim.
No production user or data migration exists.
Package name follows oya-supply-chain-planning-domain and flat microservice layout.
Machine-readable supply-chain-planning spec and existing task ledger capture the slice without creating root markdown sprawl.
The new domain crate depends only on oya-data-boundary-kernel and adds no third-party dependencies.
